transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jared (BrightCart CTO), Sara (ML), Priya (Finance), Tom (Infra)

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm aisha from redwood, i'll kick off, quick agenda: understand your workloads, cost constraints, and whether hosted / dedicated / private makes sense.
[00:12] Jared (BrightCart): thanks aisha, yeah excited — we have an ecommerce recommender + search rerank flow, want to get real unit economics before we commit.
[00:26] Marco (Redwood): hi all, marco here, i'll focus on latency/throughput knobs and the batching/caching impact on per-token cost.
[00:34] Priya (BrightCart - Finance): hi, quick note from finance side: we have a strict budget for inference, target is sub-$0.002 per inference avg if possible, but depends on tokens.
[00:50] Aisha: great, can you describe traffic? qps, average prompt/response token lengths, peak windows?
[01:05] Jared: baseline 150 qps, peaks to 500 during promos, avg prompt ~80 tokens, response ~120 tokens. Some requests are short (search rerank ~30 tokens).
[01:20] Sara: also we do session-based chat for customer support, those have longer context and kv-cache reuse.
[01:31] Marco: ok so two patterns: high-qps short-gen and lower-qps long-chat. Batching helps the short ones; kv-cache and prefix caching helps the chat flows.
[01:45] Tom (Infra): question on data residency / KMS — for Dedicated or Private we need KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:55] Aisha: yes we support KMS/HSM and have audit logs; we'll share SOC2/KMS docs after this.

[02:15] Jared: what are ballpark per-token rates for hosted vs dedicated? we saw some vendors list $0.0004/token but that's variable.
[02:29] Aisha: good question — hosted baseline depends on model family; rough example: for a mid-size open model hosted it's around $0.0003-$0.0006 per input token and similar for output, but effective cost can drop a lot with batching and caching; dedicated is usually lower unit cost but requires commit.
[02:49] Priya: commit as in reserved capacity monthly? how do we model that vs pay-as-you-go?
[02:57] Marco: dedicated is reserved GPU pools; you pay a capacity fee (monthly) + lower per-token egress/usage accounting because your amortized infra is lower. For heavy sustained qps dedicated often wins on unit economics.
[03:17] Sara: can you quantify batching benefits? we do dynamic batching client-side now but not server-side.
[03:26] Marco: yes — batching raises throughput and reduces per-token kernel overhead. For small requests, going from batch size 1 to 8 can reduce CPU/GPU overhead 30-50% depending on model/hf kernel. Continuous batching in our runtime minimizes latency penalities. Also prefix/KV caching on chat reduces decode tokens dramatically for repeated session history.
[03:50] Jared: do you have a worked example for our numbers?
[03:54] Aisha: not yet — we'll run a sim with your traffic. but high-level: assume 200 tokens total per request * 150 qps = 30k tokens/sec; if hosted price is $0.0004/token -> raw $12/sec or ~$1,036,800/month which is obviously huge; but those numbers show you need batching/caching and maybe dedicated.
[04:20] Priya: that math surprised us; we run into huge bills with some vendors.
[04:28] Marco: also consider tokenization differences and model size — a smaller quantized model could cut decode cost by 30-60% and be compatible with dedicated.

[05:00] Aisha: what are your success criteria for a pilot? cost per inference target, latency SLO, and integration effort?
[05:10] Jared: latency p50 under 120ms for search rerank, p95 under 400ms; cost ideally <$0.001 per inference avg. timeline: pilot within 4 weeks.
[05:25] Marco: for p95 we're seeing for similar workloads dedicated with optimized kernels and batching hit those latencies; hosted can as well but cost varies.

[06:00] Priya: procurement question — what contract len for dedicated? discounts for annual vs monthly?
[06:07] Aisha: standard is monthly or annual commit; annual gives deeper discounts and predictable TCO. we'll include both scenarios in the TCO sheet.

[06:30] Tom: network egress and region placement — can we put dedicated in our preferred region to reduce latency?
[06:38] Marco: yes, we support region pinning for Dedicated; Private deployment also available for full control.

[07:05] Jared: curious about fallback behavior — if dedicated pool is saturated what happens?
[07:11] Marco: smart routing can fall back to hosted region/model variant; you can configure policy: fail open to lower-cost model, route to hosted with degrade, or queue. we can demo automatic fallback.

[07:40] Aisha: ok let's step through a sample cost calc: we will run sims but here's a quick example: short gen requests batched 8x, effective token cost drops 40%; chat flows with kv-cache reuse drop decode tokens by ~60%.
[07:59] Jared: can we control caching TTL? some sessions are long but we have privacy rules.
[08:06] Marco: yes TTL and retention configurable, and audit logs show cache hits. for private deployments you control retention.

[09:00] Priya: additionally we need breakdown by token type — input vs output pricing? some vendors charge differently.
[09:07] Aisha: we show token-level breakdowns in console; pricing template will list input vs output if needed.

[09:40] Sara: technical detail — are you using flash attention kernels or custom fused kernels for attention? affects latency.
[09:46] Marco: we select kernels dynamically; for some models we use optimized fused kernels and FlashAttention paths where beneficial. we'll share perf profiles.

[10:20] Jared: security — SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
[10:27] Aisha: yes, customer-managed KMS supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports envelope encryption with KMS integration; we'll share detailed docs.

[11:00] Priya: ok from finance side we need a 3-scenario TCO: low (hosted), mid (dedicated monthly commit), high (private license + infra).
[11:10] Aisha: will do. we'll include amortized GPU costs, token price, and expected savings from batching/caching.

[12:00] Tom: for the benchmark can you run both imitation of our real traffic and a synthetic burst test? we want peak behavior.
[12:08] Marco: yes we'll run steady-state, burst, and chat reuse sims and provide token/unit cost outputs and latency percentiles.

[13:00] Jared: what data do you need from us to run sims?
[13:05] Marco: sample qps timeline (1 week), token distribution by route, target models, any session affinity rules, and any retention/TOS constraints.
[13:20] Jared: we'll share by monday.

[14:00] Aisha: quick recap of next steps: we'll send pricing sheet + TCO, SOC2/KMS docs link, schedule tech deep dive for benchmarks, and you share workload sample.
[14:12] Priya: thanks. one more: can you add a sensitivity table in the TCO for batch sizes 1/4/8/16?
[14:20] Marco: yup will include batching sensitivity and quantization options.

[15:00] Aisha: ok thanks everyone; we'll follow up in email with attachments and proposed meeting times.
[15:10] Jared: thanks all.

[END]
